review_evidence: Read developers/bench-metis-order.sml in full (4516 bytes): a metis-search-timing-variance investigation script. Despite its 'benchmark, not a permanent theorem' framing in the header comment, its body defines `val () = new_theory "bench_metis_order"`, `val axioms = <a full HOL term encoding an implicational/relevance-logic axiom system: reflexivity, prefixing, suffixing, contract3>`, and `val goals = [("assertion", ...), ("prefixing", ...), ("suffixing", ...), ("contract3", ...)]`, each a genuine logical statement.

Confirmed each goal is actually proved: `run_once` calls `prove(mk_imp(axioms, tm), strip_tac >> metis_tac[])`, a real HOL proof of each of the four goals from the axiom system, run REPEATS=6 times purely to measure metis's search-time variance (not to add a library theorem -- the new theory is not exported).

The file explicitly cross-references examples/logic/relevant-logic/SlaneyRLScript.sml (reviewed separately under unit RRU-ad9ec76e9b3b) as the canonical source the axiom/goal content is drawn from, confirming this is genuine relevant-logic formal content rather than synthetic timing-test data.

This content is distinguishable from the 12 sibling developers/*.sml files excluded by the prior review (bench-arith-cache.sml, bloom_bench.sml, core-emacs-mode.sml, genUseScript.sml, generateBuildSummary.sml, mlsysinfo.sml, mosmlTextIO.sml, mosmlgbs.sml, mosmlsysinfo.sml, poly-prehol.sml, polysysinfo.sml, prehol.sml), none of which were re-read here since they are unchanged and frozen under the brief's 'Exclusions already in force' section; this file alone was newly changed and required a fresh FILTER-004 assessment, which its content (real HOL axioms, goals, and metis-based proofs) fails to meet the exclusion bar for.

Per FILTER-022, the prior blanket 'developer/build/runtime tooling' characterization of the developers/ subtree is not automatically inherited for this newly-changed file; independent content-level assessment finds genuine formal declarations and proofs, so the file is retained.
